conventionalBriefMetric.threeAxisSeparation: Static coverage/type column in Section 7 & Section 8 dependency table
conventionalBriefMetric.clicksToInspectLocatorAndStanding: Client-side text filter or scroll across bibliography and dependency matrix (1-3 steps)

criteria.honestAssessment: A competent conventional searchable reference interface with Section 6B Argument tables and Section 8 Source-Dependency Matrices achieves 100% citation coverage, keyword searchability, and single-source lookup PARITY with OpenLine Department of History M5. M5 earns a verifiable advantage on (1) honest question boundary classification (SUPPORTED vs. PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED with explicit coverage gaps vs. UNSUPPORTED refusal on future forecasts/ideological laws, where a naive keyword search returns zero hits without explaining why or returns false-friend substring matches), and (2) live 3-axis verification + co-cited quote-attribution enforcement.

criteria.criterion: Important Differences, Omitted Context & Rejected Comparisons
criteria.honestAssessment: For reading pre-authored comparisons, argument limits, and rejected analogies, the searchable reference interface achieves PARITY with M5. M5 improves over the reference interface when a user tests a novel or hedged analogy: the live Analogy Falsifier rejects deterministic overclaims, missing breakdown limits, and structural domain mismatches.

criteria.criterion: Comparable Historical Arguments, Competing Explanations & Non-Manufactured Consensus
criteria.honestAssessment: PARITY for a reader inspecting the pre-authored historiography and Section 6B Comparable Historical Arguments table. M5's specific advantage is interactive cross-inquiry argument comparison plus runtime validation that refuses consensus-washing or incomplete argument chains.

Descriptive comprehension of documented outcomes and counterexamples is at PARITY. M5 adds active causal-discipline guardrails (refusing single-cause correlation claims, superficial keyword causation, and future predictions like 'What will happen in 2030?').

criteria.criterion: Correction Behavior After Challenged or Withdrawn Evidence

historyLabMetric.singleSourceChallenge: 1 click (<10ms) to quarantine sole-source claims and narrow multi-source claims and arguments.
historyLabMetric.multiSourceSimultaneousChallenge: Automatically computes set-intersection across simultaneously withdrawn sources across both 104 core records and 15 comparable arguments, withholding any single-source fallback text that depends on a second withdrawn source.
historyLabMetric.sqliteLedgerAudit: Mandate-Ledger hash-chained SQLite ledger records withdrawal, reopening, and re-review without rewriting prior history.

conventionalBriefMetric.automaticDependencyGraph: Static Reverse-Impact Matrix in Section 8 (searchable via toolbar)
conventionalBriefMetric.singleSourceChallenge: PARITY on single-source lookup: reader can filter or inspect the Section 8 Source-Dependency Matrix in 1 lookup to see sole-source vs. co-cited records and arguments for any single source.
conventionalBriefMetric.multiSourceSimultaneousChallenge: When 2+ sources are challenged simultaneously, reader must manually compute set intersections across multiple rows of Section 8 and manually rewrite narrowed claims.
conventionalBriefMetric.sqliteLedgerAudit: None; static reference table has no live multi-source intersection state or append-only challenge ledger.

criteria.honestAssessment: With Section 8 Source-Dependency Matrices and client-side search, the conventional searchable reference interface achieves PARITY on single-source dependency lookup. M5's genuine advantage is combinatorial multi-source withdrawal propagation across both records and comparable arguments, live text replacement in the Question-to-History briefing, and append-only SQLite/notebook state.

criteria.criterion: First-Time User Effort, Question Routing & Cognitive Load

historyLabMetric.questionFirstEntry: Ordinary-language Question-to-History console classifies SUPPORTED, PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED (with explicit missing coverage), and UNSUPPORTED (refusing future forecasts and ideological determinism) in 1 step.
historyLabMetric.linearReadingEffort: Question Briefing + Citizen Guide display relevance, comparable arguments, outcomes, and limits immediately on load.
historyLabMetric.sourceVerificationEffort: 1 click on any citation chip opens the full 3-axis Source Card in the modal inspector.

conventionalBriefMetric.questionFirstEntry: Substring search bar filters matching paragraphs (`PARITY` for exact keyword hits), but cannot distinguish supported vs. partially supported coverage gaps or explain why 'What will happen in 2030?' is refused.
conventionalBriefMetric.linearReadingEffort: 0 tab clicks (continuous vertical scroll across all 5 inquiries, slight advantage for uninterrupted linear reading).
conventionalBriefMetric.sourceVerificationEffort: Filter or scroll to Section 7/8 for source details.

criteria.honestAssessment: Continuous linear reading and exact-keyword filtering are at PARITY. M5 improves first-time citizen comprehension when asking ordinary-language questions, distinguishing partial coverage from unsupported speculation, and stress-testing sources.
